trust_decision.summary: Attacker-controlled: the `destination` and `source_path` strings deserialized from a PR-supplied `.skills.toml`, and the file tree (symlinks) of the skills library; trusted: the operator's project cwd and the library cache root. The decision is made on deserialization in `project_config::load` (`InstalledSkill::validate`, lexical components only) and again at copy time in `fs_util::copy_dir_all`/`replace_folder_contents` (symlink rejection).

landing_point.why: The summary names symlink-follow as the first defect (arbitrary file disclosure), and this is the branch where `entry.file_type()?.is_dir()` is false for a symlink so the entry falls to `fs::copy` at src/fs_util.rs:15, which dereferences it; the same helper is called from add, pull, detect and push.

fix_sites.entry_point: skillctl add | push | pull | detect (all reach it through project_config::load)
skillctl add | push | pull | detect (load-time validation gate)
shared helper for skillctl detect/push/pull and project_config
skillctl add, skillctl pull, skillctl detect (copy_dir_all top-level source)
skillctl add, skillctl pull, skillctl detect (copy_dir_all descendant entries)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: `fs_util::copy_dir_all` is a generic directory-copy helper with no knowledge of skills or `.skills.toml`, so a solver can call it infrastructure outside the advisory's config-traversal story and fix only the `destination`/`source_path` joins in push and pull.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: `.skills.toml` paths and `--target` values made only of `Normal` and `.` components must keep working, in particular `detect --target .` (library root) and `./foo` / `foo/./bar`; a fix that rejects every non-`Normal` component, or rejects `.` outright, breaks the documented flat-layout recipe and the `is_root` path.

O6_input_shapes: parent traversal at start, middle and end: `../../../etc`, `foo/../bar`, `foo/..`
empty path and bare `.` (accepted; must stay accepted, `detect --target .`)
single-component fork names exactly `.` or `..` (push and pull `validate_fork_name`)
symlink top-level source dir, symlinked file inside a tree, symlinked subdir inside a tree, symlinked replace destination
same value arriving as a TOML-deserialized PathBuf (destination/source_path) or as a clap PathBuf flag (--target)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `skillctl add`'s destination is never validated: `resolve_destination` returns `--dest` verbatim (and the interactive custom prompt only checks for emptiness), then `dest_root.join(folder_name)` is passed to `fs::remove_dir_all` on --on-conflict overwrite and to `copy_dir_all`, so `--dest /` or `--dest ../..` writes and deletes outside the project; the published fix changed detect's equivalent `--target` but not add.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: `--dest` is an explicit operator-supplied CLI flag, not a value deserialized from `.skills.toml` or shipped by the library, so it is outside the advisory's untrusted-input story.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 module dir from the landing point (src/commands/add.rs vs src/fs_util.rs), 2 files of reach (add.rs -> fs_util.rs)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Lexical-only join: `library_root.join(source_path)` and `cwd.join(destination)` are validated by components, but an intermediate directory replaced by a symlink (a library commit can flip a tracked skill folder to a symlink, which `git reset --hard` checks out) is still followed by `replace_folder_contents` -> `remove_dir_all`, and `copy_dir_all` only stats the final component.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The project documents its threat model as purely lexical and explicitly trusts the base path's parents (`path_safety`'s own note says symlinks inside copied trees are handled in `fs_util`, and `copy_dir_all` does check the entry itself), so a solver can call base-side symlinks out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/commands/pull.rs -> src/fs_util.rs, one module hop; same for push at src/commands/push.rs:320-333

O8b_injection_room.sibling: route `add --dest` through the same `validate_relative_subpath` helper detect's `--target` uses
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: add and detect are mirror commands (library<->project) with the same flag shape, and the fix added exactly this check to detect's `--target` while leaving add's `--dest` alone; README.md:121 already documents `--dest` as project-relative.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate `InstalledSkill` in `save` as well as in `load`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: push.rs:397-403 constructs a replacement `InstalledSkill` inline and save writes it unvalidated, so the invariant currently holds only on read; a maintainer hardening the type would add it here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `local_fork_destination` joins cwd with `destination.parent()` without `safe_join`, mirroring push.rs:390 which was converted
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: push and pull duplicate the fork logic (`fork_op_for_name` vs `local_fork_destination`, two copies of `validate_fork_name`); the fix hardened push's abs_old/abs_new joins but left pull's destination construction as a name check only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the interactive custom-path prompt validates only non-empty, while detect.rs:353-356 got the shared validator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the two prompts are copy-paste siblings; the fix updated one and not the other.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22) combined with symlink following (CWE-61): arbitrary file read, write and directory deletion outside the project and library roots

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate `destination` and `source_path` at the top of push::run and pull::run (reject absolute and `..` before the joins) and stop there, leaving `fs_util::copy_dir_all`'s symlink dereference and add's `--dest` untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: src/commands/init.rs:21 calls `fs::remove_dir_all` on a cache path built from the configured URL via `slug_for_url` (src/config.rs:62-84), which restricts the value to an `owner-repo` slug; not pursued.
`path_safety` accepts empty and `.` paths, so a `.skills.toml` entry with `destination = ""` resolves to the project root itself; a self-inflicted footgun rather than a traversal, not pursued.
